title: Genesis Chapter 38 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 38 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 38 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 38.

questions.question: To whom did Judah turn in when he went down from his brethren?
questions.correctAnswer: Hirah the Adullamite
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:1 states that Judah turned in to a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.

questions.question: Who was the daughter of the Canaanite that Judah took as his wife?
questions.correctAnswer: Shuah
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:2 tells us that Judah saw a daughter of a certain Canaanite, whose name was Shuah, and took her.

questions.question: What was the name of Judah and Shuah's first son?
questions.correctAnswer: Er
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:3 states that she bore a son and he called his name Er.

questions.question: Who was Judah's second son named?
questions.correctAnswer: Onan
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:4 says she conceived again and bore a son, and she called his name Onan.

questions.question: Who was the third son born to Judah's wife, and where was he born?
questions.correctAnswer: Shelah at Chezib
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:5 states she bore a son called Shelah, and he was at Chezib when she bore him.

questions.question: Who did Judah give in marriage to his firstborn Er?
questions.correctAnswer: Tamar
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:6 says Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar.

questions.question: Why did the LORD slay Er, Judah's firstborn?
options: He was wicked in the sight of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: He was wicked in the sight of the LORD
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:7 states Er was wicked in the sight of the LORD and so the LORD slew him.

questions.question: What instruction did Judah give to Onan concerning his brother's wife Tamar?
options: Go in unto thy brother's wife, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother
Send her back to her father's house
questions.correctAnswer: Go in unto thy brother's wife, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:8 records Judah telling Onan to marry Tamar and raise up seed for his brother.

questions.question: What did Onan do when he went in unto his brother's wife Tamar?
options: He spilled his seed on the ground
He married her and raised up seed
questions.correctAnswer: He spilled his seed on the ground
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:9 explains Onan spilled his seed on the ground to avoid giving seed to his brother.

questions.question: What was the LORD's reaction to Onan's actions?
options: He was displeased and slew him
questions.correctAnswer: He was displeased and slew him
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:10 says the LORD was displeased and killed Onan because of his actions.

questions.question: True or False: After Onan died, Judah told Tamar to remain a widow at her father's house until Shelah was grown.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:11 records Judah telling Tamar to remain a widow at her father's house until Shelah grew up.

questions.question: True or False: Judah's wife, the daughter of Shuah, died before Judah went up to Timnath to shear his sheep.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:12 states that the daughter of Shuah died, and then Judah was comforted and went to Timnath.

questions.question: True or False: Tamar was given to Shelah, Judah's son, as his wife as soon as he was grown.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:14 clarifies Tamar was not given to Shelah even though he was grown.

questions.question: True or False: Judah recognized Tamar when she sat by the way to Timnath covered with a veil.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:15-16 shows Judah thought she was a harlot and did not know she was Tamar.

questions.question: In Genesis 38, which event came first?
options: Judah took a wife for Er
Judah went down to Hirah the Adullamite
Judah sent a kid for a pledge
Tamar was brought forth to be burnt
questions.correctAnswer: Judah went down to Hirah the Adullamite
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:1 describes Judah going down to Hirah before any other events.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 38 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 38 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Genesis 38:11, why did Judah tell Tamar to remain a widow in her father's house?
options: Because Shelah was too young and Judah feared he might die like his brothers
Because Tamar was not worthy to marry Shelah
Because Judah wanted Tamar to remarry someone else
Because Tamar had to complete a mourning period
questions.correctAnswer: Because Shelah was too young and Judah feared he might die like his brothers
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:11 explains Judah told Tamar to remain a widow until Shelah was grown because he feared Shelah might also die like his brothers Er and Onan (Genesis 38:7, 38:10).

questions.question: What change in Judah’s household occurred in Genesis 38:12 that led him to travel to Timnath?
options: The death of the daughter of Shuah, Judah’s wife
The death of his son Er
questions.correctAnswer: The death of the daughter of Shuah, Judah’s wife
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:12 states that Judah’s wife, the daughter of Shuah, died, which comforted Judah and led him to go to Timnath with his friend Hirah.

questions.question: How does Genesis 38:13 demonstrate the connection between Tamar’s awareness and Judah’s actions?
options: Tamar was informed Judah was going to Timnath to shear his sheep, showing her awareness of Judah’s movements
Judah sent Tamar a message to meet him at Timnath
Tamar was unaware of Judah’s plans and was surprised
Judah asked Tamar to prepare a meal for the sheepshearers
questions.correctAnswer: Tamar was informed Judah was going to Timnath to shear his sheep, showing her awareness of Judah’s movements
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:13 tells that Tamar was informed of Judah’s trip to Timnath, which relates to her subsequent actions in the following verses (Genesis 38:14-16).

questions.question: What did Tamar do in Genesis 38:14 that caused Judah to mistake her for a harlot?
options: She put off her widow's garments and covered her face with a veil
She wore bright clothes and jewelry
She disguised herself as a servant
questions.correctAnswer: She put off her widow's garments and covered her face with a veil
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:14 states Tamar removed her widow's garments, covered her face with a veil, and sat openly by the way, causing Judah to mistake her for a harlot (Genesis 38:15).

questions.question: Based on Genesis 38:15, why did Judah mistake Tamar for a harlot?
options: Because she was in the city
Because she spoke to him boldly
questions.correctAnswer: Because her face was covered
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:15 explains Judah thought Tamar was a harlot because she had covered her face with a veil, hiding her identity.

questions.question: What did Judah offer to give Tamar as a pledge in Genesis 38:16-18 before they came together?
questions.correctAnswer: His signet, bracelets, and staff
questions.explanation: In Genesis 38:16-18, Tamar asked Judah for a pledge before he sent the kid from the flock, and he gave her his signet, bracelets, and staff as security.

questions.question: After the encounter with Judah, what did Tamar do according to Genesis 38:19?
options: She put on her widow’s garments again and laid aside her veil
She immediately told Judah who she was
She stayed in the open place
She went to Timnath to find Judah
questions.correctAnswer: She put on her widow’s garments again and laid aside her veil
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:19 describes Tamar arising, laying aside her veil, and putting on her widow's garments again, restoring her appearance as a widow.

questions.question: What was the outcome when Judah sent the kid to collect his pledge from Tamar as noted in Genesis 38:20?
options: The friend could not find the woman and was told there was no harlot there
Tamar returned the kid and the pledge
Tamar confessed to the friend who she was
The friend was attacked by men of the place
questions.correctAnswer: The friend could not find the woman and was told there was no harlot there
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:20-21 show that Judah’s friend could not find Tamar and was told by the men that no harlot was present in that place.

questions.question: How does Genesis 38:23 demonstrate Judah’s concern about the situation with Tamar after his friend could not find her?
options: He said to let her keep the pledge to avoid shame
He sent more men to search for her
He declared she was guilty and punished her
questions.correctAnswer: He said to let her keep the pledge to avoid shame
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:23 records Judah saying to let Tamar keep the pledge so that they would not be shamed, showing concern for both reputation and fairness.

questions.question: In Genesis 38:24, what accusation was made against Tamar, and what was Judah’s initial reaction?
options: She was accused of harlotry and pregnancy; Judah ordered her to be burnt
She was accused of theft; Judah defended her
She was accused of lying; Judah ignored it
She was accused of adultery; Judah sent her away
questions.correctAnswer: She was accused of harlotry and pregnancy; Judah ordered her to be burnt
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:24 states Tamar was accused of harlotry and pregnancy, and Judah responded by ordering her to be brought forth and burnt.

questions.question: What evidence did Tamar present to Judah to prove the father of her child in Genesis 38:25?
options: The signet, bracelets, and staff belonging to Judah
questions.correctAnswer: The signet, bracelets, and staff belonging to Judah
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:25 shows Tamar sent Judah the signet, bracelets, and staff as evidence identifying him as the father of her child.

questions.question: How did Judah respond when Tamar revealed the pledge items in Genesis 38:26, and what does this teach about humility and righteousness?
options: He acknowledged she was more righteous than him because he had not given her to Shelah
He insisted she was guilty and punished her
He denied the items belonged to him
He ignored the evidence and refused to listen
questions.correctAnswer: He acknowledged she was more righteous than him because he had not given her to Shelah
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:26 records Judah admitting Tamar was more righteous than he because he failed to give her to Shelah, demonstrating humility and acknowledgment of his fault.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 38:14, Tamar disguised herself because Shelah had grown and was given to her as husband.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:14 explicitly states Tamar saw that Shelah was grown but was not given to her as husband, which prompted her disguise.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 38:16 shows that Judah was unaware that the woman he approached was Tamar, his daughter-in-law.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:16 explains Judah did not know the woman was Tamar, his daughter-in-law, when he asked to come unto her.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 38:20-22 show that the men of the place recognized Tamar as a harlot and helped Judah's friend find her.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verses 20-22 reveal the men of the place denied that any harlot was there and the friend could not find Tamar, indicating no help was given.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 38 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 38.

questions.question: What was Judah's response when Tamar was accused of playing the harlot and being pregnant?
questions.correctAnswer: He said to burn her
questions.explanation: Judah said, 'Bring her forth, and let her be burnt' because she was accused of harlotry and pregnancy (Genesis 38:24).

questions.question: What did Tamar send to Judah as proof of the man who fathered her child?
questions.correctAnswer: The signet, bracelets, and staff
questions.explanation: Tamar sent Judah the signet, bracelets, and staff that he had given her as a pledge, to identify the father of her child (Genesis 38:25).

questions.question: How did Judah react after recognizing the items Tamar sent him?
options: He acknowledged she was more righteous
questions.correctAnswer: He acknowledged she was more righteous
questions.explanation: Judah acknowledged the items and said Tamar was more righteous than he because he had not given her to his son Shelah (Genesis 38:26).

questions.question: What significant event occurred during Tamar's labor?
options: She was visited by a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: She gave birth to twins
questions.explanation: It came to pass during her travail that Tamar had twins in her womb (Genesis 38:27).

questions.question: What was the name given to the first twin to put out his hand, and what was placed on his hand?
questions.correctAnswer: Scarlet thread; Pharez
questions.explanation: The midwife bound a scarlet thread on the hand of the first twin who put out his hand, but he drew it back, and his brother was born first and called Pharez (Genesis 38:28-29).

questions.question: Which twin was named Zarah, and why?
options: The second twin, who had the scarlet thread
The first twin, who drew back his hand
The second twin, without the scarlet thread
The first twin, with the scarlet thread
questions.correctAnswer: The second twin, who had the scarlet thread
questions.explanation: The second twin came out with the scarlet thread on his hand and was named Zarah (Genesis 38:30).

questions.question: When Judah sent his friend Hirah to retrieve the pledge from the woman, what did the men of that place say about the harlot?
options: There was no harlot in that place
She was hidden in a nearby house
questions.correctAnswer: There was no harlot in that place
questions.explanation: The men said there was no harlot in that place when Hirah asked about her (Genesis 38:21).

questions.question: What was the significance of Judah giving Tamar the signet, bracelets, and staff?
options: They served as a pledge to ensure payment
They were a common dowry gift
They were symbols of Judah's authority and identity
questions.correctAnswer: They were symbols of Judah's authority and identity
questions.explanation: The signet, bracelets, and staff were personal items symbolizing Judah’s authority and identity, used as a pledge when Tamar asked for a pledge (Genesis 38:18).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of raising up seed for a deceased brother as seen with Onan in Genesis 38?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 25:5-6
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 25:5-6 commands a brother-in-law to marry the widow of his deceased brother to raise up seed, directly relating to Onan's refusal in Genesis 38:8-9.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'harlot' in this chapter can also mean what in the cultural context of Genesis 38?
options: A woman practicing ritual prostitution or a promiscuous woman
questions.correctAnswer: A woman practicing ritual prostitution or a promiscuous woman
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term used for 'harlot' implies a woman engaged in prostitution or sexual immorality, reflecting Tamar's disguise and accusation (Genesis 38:15).

questions.question: What literary device best describes the narrative structure of Genesis 38 within the larger Joseph story in Genesis?
questions.correctAnswer: Intercalation (or a sandwich)
questions.explanation: Genesis 38 is an intercalation, a story inserted within the Joseph narrative (Genesis 37 and 39), providing thematic contrast and character development (Genesis 38:1-30).

questions.question: True or False: Judah immediately recognized Tamar when he met her disguised by a veil.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judah did not recognize Tamar because she had covered her face with a veil, and he thought she was a harlot (Genesis 38:15-16).

questions.question: True or False: Tamar's childbirth resulted in the birth of twins who played a significant role in the lineage of Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Tamar gave birth to twins, Pharez and Zarah, with Pharez becoming an ancestor of King David and Jesus, indicating the importance of this birth (Genesis 38:27-30).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage references the lineage of Jesus including Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 1:3
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:3 lists Perez, Tamar's son with Judah, in the genealogy of Jesus, connecting Genesis 38 to the New Testament lineage (Genesis 38:29).

questions.question: What cultural practice in Genesis 38 explains Judah's instruction to Onan regarding Tamar?
options: Levirate marriage to raise seed for a deceased brother
questions.correctAnswer: Levirate marriage to raise seed for a deceased brother
questions.explanation: Judah instructed Onan to marry Tamar and raise seed for his dead brother Er, reflecting the levirate marriage custom in ancient Near Eastern culture (Genesis 38:8).

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 38 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 38 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by the deaths of Er and Onan as recorded in Genesis 38:7-10?
options: The doctrine of divine judgment on sin
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine judgment on sin
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:7-10 shows that God executed judgment on Er and Onan because of their wickedness and disobedience, emphasizing divine holiness and justice. This aligns with God's righteous judgment seen elsewhere (Romans 1:18).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is primarily demonstrated by the LORD's actions in slaying Er and Onan (Genesis 38:7,10)?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: The LORD's act of slaying Er and Onan for their wickedness (Genesis 38:7,10) reveals His attribute of justice, showing God as a righteous judge who punishes sin.

questions.question: How does Judah's interaction with Tamar in Genesis 38:14-18 contribute to the biblical theme of redemption?
options: It illustrates God's providential use of flawed human actions to bring about His redemptive plan
It condemns all deceit as unforgivable sin
It shows that redemption is only for the righteous
It highlights the rejection of covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God's providential use of flawed human actions to bring about His redemptive plan
questions.explanation: In Genesis 38:14-18, Tamar's disguise and Judah's unknowing involvement show how God can use imperfect human behavior within His sovereign plan to preserve the Messianic line, a theme of redemption through unlikely means.

questions.question: What theological significance does the birth of twins Pharez and Zarah in Genesis 38:27-30 hold?
options: It signifies God's sovereign election and the unexpected fulfillment of His covenant promises
It teaches that birth order always determines leadership
It demonstrates the failure of human lineage
It shows the importance of legal marriage only
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies God's sovereign election and the unexpected fulfillment of His covenant promises
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:27-30 records the birth of twins where the younger, Pharez, is born first, illustrating God's sovereign election overriding human customs and advancing His covenant plan, as also seen in Romans 9:10-13.

questions.question: What combined teaching about God's providence and human responsibility is conveyed by Genesis 38:11 and Genesis 38:24-26 regarding Tamar's situation?
options: God's providence uses human actions and decisions, even failures, to accomplish His righteous purposes
Human actions are irrelevant to God's plan
God punishes all human failures without exception
Providence negates the need for human obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence uses human actions and decisions, even failures, to accomplish His righteous purposes
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:11 shows Judah withholding Shelah from Tamar, and 38:24-26 shows Tamar taking matters into her own hands. Together, they reveal God's providence working through human failures and decisions to fulfill His righteous purposes.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Genesis 38:1-2 establish in the broader redemptive history of Scripture?
options: It introduces Judah's line, which will culminate in the Messianic lineage
It shifts focus away from Israel to Gentile nations
It ends God's covenant with Abraham
It shows the failure of all patriarchs
questions.correctAnswer: It introduces Judah's line, which will culminate in the Messianic lineage
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:1-2 sets the stage for Judah's lineage, central to the Messianic promise, linking to the broader redemptive story culminating in Christ (Matthew 1:3-16).

questions.question: Skeptics claim that the story of Judah and Tamar in Genesis 38 promotes immoral behavior. What does Genesis 38:13-26 actually teach about God's righteousness and justice?
options: God upholds justice and righteousness even through complex human situations, vindicating the righteous and condemning sin
God condones all human actions without judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God upholds justice and righteousness even through complex human situations, vindicating the righteous and condemning sin
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:13-26 shows Tamar's cunning to secure her rightful place and Judah's eventual acknowledgment of her righteousness, reflecting God's justice and vindication amid human complexity.

questions.question: Which doctrine is exemplified by Judah's acknowledgment in Genesis 38:26 that Tamar was 'more righteous' than he?
options: The doctrine of repentance and confession
The doctrine of justification by works
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of repentance and confession
questions.explanation: Judah's confession (Genesis 38:26) reveals the biblical doctrine of repentance and acknowledgment of sin, a key step toward restoration and righteousness.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by the LORD's sovereign control over human fertility and lineage in Genesis 38:3-5 and 38:27-30?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: God's control over the conception and birth of Er, Onan, Shelah, and later the twins Pharez and Zarah (Genesis 38:3-5, 27-30) reveals His sovereignty over human history and covenant promises.

questions.question: How does the narrative in Genesis 38:6-11 contribute to the biblical teaching on levirate marriage and covenant responsibility?
options: It teaches the importance of raising offspring for deceased brothers to preserve family lineage
It forbids marriage within extended families
It promotes polygamy as a covenant duty
It denies any obligation to deceased relatives
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches the importance of raising offspring for deceased brothers to preserve family lineage
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:6-11 shows Judah instructing Onan to marry Tamar to raise seed for Er, illustrating the levirate marriage principle to preserve family lineage and covenant promises.

questions.question: What synthesis of doctrine is taught by combining the events of Genesis 38:8-10 with Genesis 38:24-26 regarding divine judgment and human justice?
options: God's judgment on sin is righteous, but human justice requires discernment and mercy
God ignores human sin and leaves it to humans to judge
Human justice is always harsh and vindictive
Divine judgment always ignores human circumstances
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment on sin is righteous, but human justice requires discernment and mercy
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:8-10 shows God's righteous judgment on Onan's sin, while 38:24-26 reveals human misjudgment of Tamar, teaching the need for wise human justice within divine righteousness.

questions.question: What does Genesis 38:20-23 teach about human limitations in discerning God's providence?
options: Humans often fail to perceive God's workings and can misunderstand situations
Humans have full understanding of divine plans
God reveals all future events clearly to mankind
Providence is always obvious to human observers
questions.correctAnswer: Humans often fail to perceive God's workings and can misunderstand situations
questions.explanation: In Genesis 38:20-23, Judah's inability to find Tamar and the men denying a harlot's presence show human limitations in recognizing God's providence and the complexity of His plans.

questions.question: How does Genesis 38:12-14 demonstrate God's providential timing in the unfolding of His redemptive plan?
options: God's timing brings events to fulfillment when the time is right, as with Tamar waiting until Shelah was grown
Events happen only by human initiative
questions.correctAnswer: God's timing brings events to fulfillment when the time is right, as with Tamar waiting until Shelah was grown
questions.explanation: Genesis 38:12-14 shows Tamar's patient waiting and then taking action when Judah goes to Timnath, illustrating God's providential timing in redemptive history.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by synthesizing Judah's actions in Genesis 38:1-2 and his later recognition of Tamar's righteousness in Genesis 38:26?
options: God's grace can work through flawed individuals to fulfill His covenant promises
Only perfect people are used by God
God rejects the lineage of sinners
questions.correctAnswer: God's grace can work through flawed individuals to fulfill His covenant promises
questions.explanation: Judah's initial flawed decisions (Genesis 38:1-2) and later confession of Tamar's righteousness (38:26) together show how God's grace redeems flawed humanity to preserve His covenant.

questions.question: What does the story of Onan's refusal to raise seed for his brother in Genesis 38:9-10 reveal about the sanctity of covenant obligations?
options: Covenant responsibilities are sacred and disobedience results in divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant responsibilities are sacred and disobedience results in divine judgment
questions.explanation: Onan's refusal to fulfill his levirate duty (Genesis 38:9-10) and subsequent death show that covenant obligations have sacred importance and disobedience incurs God’s judgment.
